decisions: A lease-guarded route validates its bearer at the policy boundary before the handler runs; plan 02-09 adds the second, decisive check inside the coordinator lock.
A filtered collection is reachable by every authenticated principal and protected by omitting rows; refusing the call would itself leak that rows exist.
Component-wide surfaces authorize against the union of a principal's project capabilities; a user with no assignment anywhere still holds nothing.
Authorization is decided synchronously at the WebSocket boundary, before a handler is scheduled.
Each RED test file carries exactly one product-completeness sentinel and reports every unmet guarantee as a gap list, so a controlled RED fails exactly once.
No release is created at this checkpoint.
Live Home Assistant, remote-site, physical-bus, and plant writes remain outside authorization.

The browser never derives a role-to-capability matrix of its own. Until the server returns one, RoleMatrixDisclosure renders its declared unavailable state: a client-side matrix would be exactly the browser-derived authority this phase exists to prevent.
A threat row is marked verified only after its owner command has actually run and passed. T2-16 stays planned rather than being marked on the strength of its constituent parts passing separately.

Vocabulary data lives in schemas/vocabularies.json beside limits.json rather than in a foreign x-vocabularies keyword inside the schema: a foreign keyword is something every consumer has to be taught about, and it breaks Ajv strict mode. A drift test asserts the schema enums equal these keys.
A profile control is deny-default via unevaluatedProperties: false, so it cannot name a domain, service or target at all; the server still resolves every control from the verified head.

Entity mapping is an assignment problem, not a per-slot ranking: a candidate that fully covers another slot's name is skipped for this slot. An undeclared role token is an eligibility rule, not a score penalty.
The containment path is derived from the hierarchy rather than stored, so it cannot drift from the graph it describes.
Provenance is project-scoped and describes only entities the project references, so the route cannot become a registry search; a hidden project answers byte-identically to a missing one.
